blocks.text: This chapter presents short, sharply contrasted sayings about wisdom and folly, work and poverty, speech and conduct, righteousness and wickedness. Read these as compressed, context-sensitive generalizations rather than as exceptionless promises that describe every situation. For example, verse 4 commends diligence, but the wider wisdom tradition also recognizes that poverty can involve injustice and oppression; it does not reduce every person’s circumstances to personal effort alone. The opening heading associates this collection with Solomon, while the received book also contains material from other collections and teachers.

“Love covereth all transgressions” contrasts love with hatred that stirs up conflict. In this wisdom setting, covering wrongdoing can describe communal forbearance rather than fueling strife. It cannot mean concealing abuse, destroying evidence, silencing survivors, or avoiding safeguarding reports.

sections.title: A Question About Love and Conflict
